title: Implement the DASH diet using the plate method for hypertension
recommendation: Teach patients with hypertension the DASH diet using the plate method: fill half the plate with fruits and vegetables, one quarter with whole grains, and one quarter with lean protein. Specifically instruct patients to include 4-5 servings each of fruits and vegetables daily, limit sodium to 2,300mg/day, and replace salt with herbs and spices. Provide a 3-day sample meal plan with grocery list.
implementation: Provide visual DASH diet guides during counseling sessions. Create a specific 3-day meal plan tailored to patient preferences. Schedule follow-up at 2 weeks to review food diary and adjust recommendations. Provide a list of specific herb/spice combinations to replace salt.
expected_outcomes: Average systolic BP reduction of 8-14 mmHg when combined with sodium restriction. Improved overall cardiovascular risk profile. Potential reduction in antihypertensive medication needs.
target_population: Adults with hypertension or elevated blood pressure (systolic BP 120-129 mmHg and diastolic BP <80 mmHg).
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost dietary intervention that may reduce medication needs. Each 10 mmHg reduction in systolic BP is associated with 20% reduction in major cardiovascular events, saving approximately $1,000-$2,000 per patient annually.

title: Implement home BP monitoring with specific recording protocol
recommendation: Prescribe home blood pressure monitoring with a specific recording protocol: measure BP twice in the morning and twice in the evening for 7 consecutive days. Instruct patients to record all values with date and time, calculate the average of all readings (excluding the first day), and bring the log to their next appointment. Demonstrate proper technique during the office visit.
implementation: Provide a standardized BP log sheet. Verify patients have validated BP devices or provide resources to obtain one. Schedule a follow-up visit specifically to review home readings. Set up EHR templates to document home BP averages separately from office readings.
expected_outcomes: More accurate assessment of true BP with 50-60% reduction in white coat hypertension misdiagnosis. Better medication titration decisions. Improved patient engagement in BP management.
target_population: Adults with newly diagnosed or uncontrolled hypertension, suspected white coat or masked hypertension, or those requiring medication adjustments.
cost_effectiveness: Moderate initial cost for BP device ($50-$100), offset by reduced office visits and more targeted medication management. Each prevented cardiovascular event saves approximately $18,000-$30,000 in healthcare costs.

title: Implement the 5 A's framework for smoking cessation counseling
recommendation: Implement the 5 A's framework for smoking cessation counseling: Ask about tobacco use at every visit, Advise all tobacco users to quit with clear, personalized messages, Assess willingness to quit within the next 30 days, Assist with developing a quit plan including pharmacotherapy if appropriate, and Arrange follow-up within 1 week of the quit date.
implementation: Incorporate tobacco screening questions in intake forms. Create EHR templates for the 5 A's framework. Stock patient education materials on cessation strategies. Establish referral pathways to quitlines and cessation programs. Schedule dedicated follow-up visits or calls for quit dates.
expected_outcomes: Increased quit attempts by 30-40%. Improved long-term cessation rates of 15-30% when combined with pharmacotherapy. Reduced cardiovascular and cancer risk.
target_population: All patients who use tobacco products, with priority for those with tobacco-related diseases or risk factors.
cost_effectiveness: Highly cost-effective intervention with return on investment of $2-$3 for every $1 spent. Each successful quitter saves approximately $22,000 in lifetime healthcare costs.

title: Implement the PHQ-2 to PHQ-9 depression screening sequence
recommendation: Implement a two-step depression screening process: first administer the PHQ-2 asking about 'little interest or pleasure in doing things' and 'feeling down, depressed, or hopeless' over the past two weeks (scored 0-3 for each). If score is ≥3, administer the full PHQ-9. Document exact scores and specific positive responses, not just total scores.
implementation: Incorporate PHQ-2 into routine vital signs workflow. Have PHQ-9 forms readily available for positive screens. Program EHR templates to document individual question responses. Establish clear protocols for positive screens based on score ranges. Schedule follow-up within 2 weeks for positive screens.
expected_outcomes: Identification of depression with 80-90% sensitivity and 70-85% specificity. Earlier intervention for depression. Reduced suicide risk through systematic identification of suicidal ideation (question 9).
target_population: All adult patients, with annual screening recommended. Higher-risk populations include those with chronic medical conditions, pain, substance use disorders, or recent major life changes.
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with high return on investment. Each case of depression treated in primary care saves approximately $2,000-$5,000 compared to untreated depression costs.

title: Implement the FRAX tool with specific follow-up thresholds
recommendation: Calculate 10-year fracture risk using the FRAX tool for all women ≥65 and men ≥70 years. Use country-specific calculators and input exact height, weight, and risk factors. Implement specific follow-up thresholds: if 10-year hip fracture risk is ≥3% or major osteoporotic fracture risk is ≥20%, order DXA scan and initiate fall risk assessment.
implementation: Integrate FRAX calculator into EHR or use mobile app during visits. Document calculated risks in a standardized location. Create order sets that include DXA and fall risk assessment for patients meeting thresholds. Schedule bone health follow-up visits to review results and treatment options.
expected_outcomes: Identification of high fracture risk patients with 70-80% sensitivity. Earlier intervention with appropriate therapies. Reduction in hip fractures by 20-40% with treatment of high-risk individuals.
target_population: Women ≥65 years and men ≥70 years, or younger patients with significant risk factors for osteoporosis or fractures.
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening tool that guides resource utilization. Each hip fracture prevented saves approximately $43,000 in direct healthcare costs.

title: Implement the AUDIT-C alcohol screening with specific follow-up
recommendation: Screen for unhealthy alcohol use using the 3-question AUDIT-C tool. Score each question 0-4 points and implement specific follow-up thresholds: for scores 4-7 (men) or 3-7 (women), provide brief counseling using the 5 A's framework; for scores ≥8, evaluate for alcohol use disorder using the full AUDIT and consider referral to specialized treatment.
implementation: Incorporate AUDIT-C into annual wellness visits. Create EHR templates with built-in scoring and follow-up recommendations. Develop brief intervention scripts based on score ranges. Establish referral relationships with addiction treatment providers. Schedule follow-up within 4 weeks for high-risk patients.
expected_outcomes: Identification of unhealthy alcohol use with 80% sensitivity and specificity. Reduction in alcohol consumption by 3-4 drinks per week with brief interventions. Earlier identification and treatment of alcohol use disorders.
target_population: All adults, with annual screening recommended. Higher-risk populations include young adults, those with mental health conditions, and those with alcohol-related medical conditions.
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with high return on investment. Each $1 spent on screening and brief intervention saves approximately $4 in healthcare and social costs.

title: Implement the STEADI algorithm for fall prevention
recommendation: Implement the STEADI (Stopping Elderly Accidents, Deaths & Injuries) algorithm: 1) Ask all patients 65+ years three key questions: Have you fallen in the past year? Do you feel unsteady when standing or walking? Do you worry about falling? 2) For any 'yes' response, perform the Timed Up and Go test, measuring the exact seconds required to rise from a chair, walk 10 feet, turn, return, and sit down. 3) If time exceeds 12 seconds, implement multifactorial interventions including medication review, vision check, and home safety evaluation.
implementation: Incorporate STEADI screening questions into Medicare Annual Wellness Visits. Train staff on proper Timed Up and Go test administration. Create EHR templates with decision support based on results. Develop order sets for positive screens. Schedule dedicated follow-up for high-risk patients.
expected_outcomes: Identification of fall risk with 85% sensitivity. Reduction in falls by 25-40% with multifactorial interventions. Decreased fall-related injuries and hospitalizations.
target_population: Adults aged 65+ years, particularly those with history of falls, mobility impairments, multiple medications, or chronic conditions affecting balance.
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with high return on investment. Each fall prevented saves approximately $14,000 in direct medical costs. Implementation costs are offset by Medicare reimbursement for fall risk assessment.

citation.title: Development of STEADI: A Fall Prevention Resource for Health Care Providers

title: Implement the 4 Ms framework for age-friendly care
recommendation: Implement the 4 Ms framework at every geriatric visit: 1) What Matters - ask 'What matters most to you when thinking about your health care?' and document the exact response, 2) Medication - review for potentially inappropriate medications using the Beers criteria, 3) Mentation - screen for depression, dementia, and delirium using validated tools, 4) Mobility - assess using the Timed Up and Go test and document exact time in seconds.
implementation: Create a 4 Ms template in the EHR. Train all team members on their roles in the framework. Schedule longer visits for comprehensive assessments. Develop protocols for positive findings in each domain. Document 4 Ms assessment in a consistent location for trending over time.
expected_outcomes: Improved patient satisfaction and engagement. Reduction in polypharmacy and adverse drug events by 15-30%. Earlier identification of cognitive impairment and mobility limitations. Better alignment of care with patient goals and values.
target_population: Adults aged 65+ years, particularly those with multiple chronic conditions, functional impairments, or recent hospitalizations.
cost_effectiveness: Moderate implementation costs offset by reduced adverse events and hospitalizations. Each prevented adverse drug event saves approximately $2,000-$7,000 in healthcare costs.

title: Implement the BATHE technique for psychosocial assessment
recommendation: Implement the BATHE technique during primary care visits by asking these exact questions in sequence: 1) Background - 'What is going on in your life right now?', 2) Affect - 'How do you feel about that?', 3) Trouble - 'What troubles you the most about this situation?', 4) Handling - 'How are you handling that?', 5) Empathy - Respond with an empathetic statement such as 'That sounds really difficult' before transitioning to medical concerns.
implementation: Train all providers on the BATHE technique. Create EHR templates with the five questions. Allocate 2-3 minutes at the beginning of visits for BATHE. Document key responses, particularly to the 'Trouble' and 'Handling' questions. Use responses to guide referrals to behavioral health resources.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of psychosocial concerns with 75-85% sensitivity. Enhanced patient satisfaction and therapeutic alliance. More efficient visits with focused attention on patient priorities.
target_population: All adult patients, particularly those with chronic conditions, unexplained physical symptoms, frequent visits, or known psychosocial stressors.
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention requiring minimal additional time. Each mental health condition identified and treated in primary care saves approximately $1,500-$3,000 compared to untreated conditions or emergency interventions.

title: Implement the SBIRT protocol for substance use screening
recommendation: Implement the SBIRT (Screening, Brief Intervention, Referral to Treatment) protocol: 1) Screen all patients annually using the AUDIT-C for alcohol and the DAST-10 for drugs, 2) For positive screens, conduct a Brief Intervention using motivational interviewing techniques and the readiness ruler ('On a scale of 1-10, how ready are you to make a change?'), 3) Refer patients with AUDIT scores ≥16 or DAST-10 scores ≥6 to specialized treatment with warm handoff when possible.
implementation: Incorporate screening tools into intake forms. Train all providers in brief intervention techniques. Create EHR templates with built-in scoring and decision support. Establish referral relationships with treatment providers. Schedule follow-up within 2-4 weeks for patients receiving brief interventions.
expected_outcomes: Identification of substance use disorders with 80-90% sensitivity. Reduction in substance use by 20-40% with brief interventions. Increased treatment engagement for those with severe disorders.
target_population: All adult patients, with annual screening recommended. Higher-risk populations include young adults, those with mental health conditions, chronic pain, or history of trauma.
cost_effectiveness: Moderate implementation costs offset by substantial healthcare savings. Each $1 invested in SBIRT saves approximately $4-$7 in healthcare and social costs.
